body:
PROBLEM (hit twice on 2026-08-14, PRs #494 and #497): once a ticket that declares rails merges to the base, `checkRailEdits` (packages/rails-guard/lib/rails.mjs) flags ANY changed file matching the rail globs — including the CREATION of a rail test file that does not exist yet. The rails-guard CI design provides no lift: T36 auto-expires rails only via `completed: true`, a PR may complete only RAILLESS tickets (isCompletionAnnotationOnly, packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs), and the #141 trust-root ceremony explicitly never lifts ticket rails. Net effect: merging a railed ticket before its build makes the build PR's rails-guard structurally red, and both seam builds had to be merged over a failing advisory check — the exact signal-erosion the gate exists to prevent. In-session, the PreToolUse hook has a sanctioned bypass (ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS) for authoring a new rail; CI has no equivalent.

BUILD

Sanction exactly the authoring act, nothing wider. In the CI rail-freeze path (packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs + lib/rails.mjs), a changed file is EXEMPT from rail-edit denial when ALL hold:
1. the file did NOT exist at the trusted base (git status A against the trusted base — an addition, never an edit/rename/delete; rename sources still deny),
2. every rail glob it matches belongs to base tickets that are NOT completed (an in-flight ticket's rail being authored; a completed ticket's rails have expired anyway and never reach the union),
3. the addition is reported in the gate's output as a sanctioned rail-authoring event naming the ticket id(s), so the PR record shows it explicitly.
Everything else is unchanged: edits, renames, deletions of existing rail files stay denied; a file that exists at base always denies; trust-root paths are untouched by this exemption (ticket rails only).

SECURITY ARGUMENT the builder must preserve and the reviewer must check: the first ADD of a declared-but-nonexistent rail path IS the sanctioned P3 authoring act — identical in kind to the in-session bypass, but narrower (addition only). An attacker planting a hollow rail test via the addition faces the same defenses the in-session path already relies on: P5 prosecution, the mutation gate, and cross-model review. What the freeze protects — an existing rail's content — remains frozen.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- AC1: fixture — base ticket declares a rail glob on a path absent at base; a PR ADDS that file → rail-freeze passes and the output names the sanctioned authoring with the ticket id. Verify: new test in packages/rails-guard/test/, named in the build.
- AC2: a second PR EDITING that now-existing file → denied (rail-edit), unchanged behavior. Verify: same test file.
- AC3: renaming or deleting an existing rail file → denied, including the rename SOURCE. Verify: same test file.
- AC4: an addition matching BOTH a ticket rail and an immutable trust root → still denied (the exemption never applies to trust roots). Verify: same test file.
- AC5: suite green: npm test.

NOTES FOR THE BUILDER

- Re-verify the current checkRailEdits/rail-freeze wiring before building (this area changed in #500's floor-hardening).
- Enforcement-package change: tiers trust-root, needs a distinct-provider cross-model approve.
- No rails declared here (this ticket is the fix for why that ordering wedges); freeze tests in-session during the build.
title: rails-guard-ci: sanction rail-file ADDITION by the declaring ticket's own build PR
